svg.title: Hierarchical Sparse Indexer: candidate pool and reindex selection
svg.desc: Layer 20 scores every visible position once, keeps the top 2048 blocks of 8 by block maximum, and publishes their union as a shared candidate pool. Layers 24, 28, 32 and 36 rescore with their own query inside that pool and keep their own top 512 positions. Blocks are never re-selected.
svg.text: Hierarchical Sparse Indexer: candidate pool and reindex selection
One full-range scan at layer 20 fixes a block-level pool. Layers 24, 28, 32 and 36 re-rank positions inside it with their own query.
Layer 20 is the only full-range scan and the only block selector. Four Reindex layers rescore inside its pool; every other layer just inherits addresses.
identical formula in every indexer layer; query and head weights differ
32 heads x 128 dims, from shared latent
one signed scalar per head, no softmax
H_I = 32, d_I = 128, so the scale is 1/64. ReLU acts on the dot product only:
the head weight may be negative, so the score may be negative and is not a probability.
Layer 20 makes two independent selections from one score vector
position kept in this layer Top-K
block kept by its maximum score
Drawn with b = 8, 12 blocks, M = 4 kept blocks, K = 3. The real configuration is b = 8, M = 2048, K = 512, so the pool holds at most 16384 positions.
Full range, unmasked. K = min(512, entries).
Local code only. Uses one of the M slots.
D. Union of the top M blocks
Whole blocks enter, positions stay separate.
The two outputs come from the same score vector but neither is derived from the other: the pool is not built out of the Top-K, and the Top-K is not restricted to the pool.
Reindex layers re-rank inside the pool. They never re-select blocks
top score at layer 24, but block B5 was dropped at layer 20: not reachable
masked_fill on the shared candidate mask
same selection semantics once the pool holds K
never the available blocks. Only layer 20
runs block selection; it is not repeated
They inherit the last address set, but
still use their own attention query;
The four Reindex layers generally return four different address sets. Nothing forces them to be nested, and each one is a subset of the same pool.
The pool preserves the source ranking, not every deeper ranking
Holds: the source layer never loses its own Top-K
A top-K position sits in a block whose maximum is at least its own score, so its block cannot
be outdone by M - 1 others. Needs no ties and more visible blocks than M. The shipped
configuration gives 2047 >= 512 with the pinned block already paid for.
Fails: a deeper layer can rank an excluded position first
b = 2, M = 2, K = 1, pinned last block
Pool = {0, 1, 6, 7}. Position 4 scores 12 at the deeper layer but its block was never kept,
so the restricted search has to fall back to position 0 and its score of 8.
What the pool buys, and where the saving stops
fewer positions scored by one Reindex layer
on decoder indexing, the five layers together
on backbone indexing, encoder scans included
Two limits: the first full scan and the encoder indexers are untouched, so the backbone ratio tends to 2.6, not 64. And prefill still forms N(N+1)/2 visible query-position pairs at that first scan.
In the released code the mask is applied after a full-width dot product, so the local run reproduces the selection, not the arithmetic saving.
